captured: 2026-11-15, 1440x900, homepage only (currently a single-product campaign page)

spacing.notes: Every measured length is a multiple of u: grid row gap 2u, list gap 3u, footer padding 4.5u x 9u, radius 1u. The whole page scales with width instead of snapping at breakpoints.

typography.case: all navigation and footer text set lowercase

colors.role: colour only inside product photography (orange controls)

motion.notes: Hover = 150-200ms colour swap; image sequence crossfades 500ms ease-out. No keyframe animations, no WAAPI animations running.

nav.structure: 5 inline columns: line pictogram (~42x84px, ~1px stroke) + lowercase word + 2-3 lowercase sub-links visible at rest

taste.name: One unit owns every length
taste.trigger: When setting spacing, radius and type across a page that must work from phone to wall display
taste.decision: Chose a single width-derived unit (1/196 of viewport) with multiples 1, 2, 3, 4.5, 9 over a fixed 4/8px scale with breakpoint overrides
taste.reason: Because when the gaps, corners and type all move together, the layout keeps the same proportions on any screen and reads as one object, like a product drawing

taste.name: Brand carried by line pictograms, not colour
taste.trigger: When building navigation that must also carry identity
taste.decision: Chose a hand-drawn single-stroke pictogram beside each lowercase section word over a coloured logo bar, icon font or dropdown menu
taste.reason: Because a set of drawings with one stroke weight is recognisable at a glance and impossible to mistake for a template, while costing zero colour
evidence: 5 nav columns each = pictogram + word + 2-3 sub-links

taste.name: No chrome around the product
taste.trigger: When presenting hardware on the homepage
taste.decision: Chose full-bleed 1:1 renders on pure black with no cards, shadows or borders over a framed product card grid
taste.reason: Because the object is the proof: anything drawn around it competes with the thing people came to look at

taste.name: Thin, lowercase voice
taste.trigger: When setting the typographic tone for a hardware company
taste.decision: Chose weight 100 lowercase text in one custom face over bold uppercase technical labelling
taste.reason: Because a quiet, lowercase voice makes precise engineering feel approachable rather than intimidating
evidence: all nav and footer labels lowercase
letter-spacing normal; uppercase only in the one-off campaign face
